text:
amina: Kicking off a lightweight dry-run for cross-project KMS grants + admin cleanup next week. Focus: identify principals with admin/owner roles plus any out-of-project KMS grants. Want to validate our attestations flow before any mass revokes.

trent: Whats the exact definition for "out-of-project KMS grant" here? We have accidental grants where a service account in project-a is granted `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on key in project-b.

amina: Exactly that. Heuristic: principal.project != key.project AND grant age > 90 days AND no recorded last_active in last 90 days. We'll tag `crossproj_kms` in the report.

luca: Please include SA key usage history check. Example cmd: 

```
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"svc-xyz@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com\" AND resource.type=\"service_account\"" --freshness=365d --format=json
```

sec-auditor: Ops-bot dry scan posted 82 candidates. 12 are cross-project KMS grants, 6 have recent key usage, 4 are linked from external vendor IPs. Report: https://internal/reports/access/1810005555 :rotating_light:

ops-bot: automated-scan: candidates=82, crossproj_kms=12, recent_key_usage=6, external_ip_links=4. report_url=https://internal/reports/access/1810005555

amina: For the 6 with recent usage, we'll mark `hold_active_kms`. For the 4 external links, tag `security-review` and notify SecOps. For the rest, schedule attestations to owners.

trent: How are we notifying owners? We should use the owner-attest GitHub workflow so we have audit proof (owner must click a link to confirm). If they don't respond in 72h, escalate to manager.

luca: Suggest adding an automated IAM snapshot step to the pipeline so we can replay restores: 
1) export iam bindings per project
2) export kms policy per key
3) stash to encrypted bucket `gs://redwood-prune-snapshots/$TS/` with retention 180d

amina: Agreed. We will also create a temporary recovery role `prune-temp-admin` granted to a small ops group for emergency reinstates. That role creation + use must be recorded in a ticket.

sec-auditor: Reminder: Any revoke touching KMS grants must trigger key-rotation playbook if the principal is a long-running service account. We cannot silently break backup pipelines.

amina: Can we get a canary plan? Proposal: pick 8 principals with low blast radius (non-prod, single-project keys) and actually revoke in canary window 2026-07-14 14:00-17:00 UTC, monitor 6h.

trent: +1. Add a dashboard `prune-canary` with spikes in 'kms.decrypt_failure' and service-account errors. Alert if decrypt_failure rate >0.05% absolute increase.

luca: Also add an automated smoke that attempts decrypt and sign operations for affected keys pre/post revoke to validate expected outcomes. Script: `./tools/kms_smoke.sh --key=$KEY --service-account=$SA`.

ops-bot: canary_candidates=8, canary_window=2026-07-14T14:00:00Z, monitor_window=6h, smoke_script=tools/kms_smoke.sh

sec-auditor: Runbook snippet for emergency restore: 
- action: add `prune-temp-admin` to project IAM binding using snapshot file
- verify: run smoke decrypt/sign tests in 5m
- audit: attach ticket and gcloud command used to change binding
- timeline: target RTO 15m, escalate to oncall if >15m

amina: Final ask: anyone with explicit objections to being included in dry-run reply with principal and reason. We'll PR the runbook tomorrow and drop the dry-run report in this thread once available. :thumbsup:

trent: Will review the 12 cross-project grants and flag any vendor-owned principals.

luca: I'll wire the snapshot + smoke into the CI pipeline and push the workflow for owner-attestations.

sec-auditor: I'll prepare the key-rotation checklist and vendor contact list for the flagged external links.

ops-bot: next_step: export_report -> owner_attest workflow -> canary_revokes -> monitor -> broader_prune (if OK)

amina: thanks team. Leaving this thread open for objections and for me to post the dry-run CSV shortly.
